title: Obsidian Word Mode
subtitle: Word-style Editor Plugin for Obsidian
description: An Obsidian plugin for editing Markdown notes like a Word document, with a ribbon toolbar, tables and images, while the file on disk stays clean Markdown. For people who know Markdown and would still rather click Bold.
longDescription: Word Mode adds a second editor for Markdown notes in Obsidian: you see formatted text instead of Markdown syntax and format with toolbar buttons and familiar word-processor shortcuts. Files stay plain Markdown. When a note is edited, only the changed blocks are written again and everything else is kept character for character; anything it cannot edit visually, such as HTML blocks, is shown as a raw block and saved unchanged. It covers a ribbon toolbar with Home, Insert, Review and View tabs, in-place tables, a properties form, images, links, find and replace, an outline sidebar, formatting as you type, Mermaid diagrams with a diagram editor, a visual equation editor, embeds, footnotes, callouts and task lists, plus a choice of versions when a note changes on disk during unsaved edits. The interface comes in Traditional Chinese, English, Japanese and Korean. It is written in TypeScript on ProseMirror and markdown-it, bundled with esbuild, and tested with editing tests that simulate Obsidian in jsdom and a read-only round trip over a real vault. No telemetry, and it never touches files outside the vault.
features: Ribbon toolbar with Home, Insert, Review and View tabs
Only changed blocks are rewritten; the rest of the file stays character for character
Tables edited in place, including sorting and pasting cells from a spreadsheet
Properties as a form, with tags and links as chips
Images you can paste, pick and resize by dragging
Formatting as you type, with each change as its own undo step
Mermaid diagrams with a diagram editor, and a visual equation editor
Embeds, footnotes, callouts and task lists with custom statuses
Find and replace, outline sidebar and heading folding
Sync conflict handling when a note changes on disk during unsaved edits
Interface in Traditional Chinese, English, Japanese and Korean
challenges: Editing notes visually without changing the Markdown the user didn't touch
Testing an editor that only runs inside Obsidian
Relying on Obsidian APIs that aren't public
solutions: Only blocks that changed are serialized again, and a read-only round trip over a real vault (notExact and lossyBlocks must both be 0) guards the converter
Editing tests simulate Obsidian with jsdom, and ESLint runs the rules Obsidian uses to review community plugins
Non-public APIs are declared in one place, each optional and checked before use; the obsidian typings are pinned to the minimum supported app version
results: Notes stay clean Markdown; anything it can't edit visually is saved unchanged
Released on GitHub; install by copying three files into the vault's plugins folder
No telemetry, no account, and no files touched outside the vault
why: In Obsidian, formatting a note still means Markdown syntax; even the shortcuts just type the symbols for you. Word Mode lets you work with toolbar buttons and word-processor shortcuts on the same .md files, and writes back only the blocks you changed, so fixing one typo doesn't turn into a diff of the whole note.
gains: Someone who has never typed a Markdown asterisk can work in the same vault: tables, properties, images, diagrams and equations all have buttons. The files stay ordinary .md, so sync and other tools never learn that someone switched editors.

lessons: The release tag must match the version exactly, with no v in front, because Obsidian looks for a release under that exact tag.
Keep the source folder and node_modules out of folders a sync client watches, such as Synology Drive.
Not checked yet: mobile use on real devices, and the Japanese and Korean translations by native speakers.
